about:
Ryobi Die Casting (USA), Inc. operates a die casting campus in Shelbyville, Indiana. The facility is part of the Ryobi Group, headquartered in Japan, which runs 11 manufacturing plants across six countries. The U.S. subsidiary employs more than 700 people at its Shelbyville location.

The company specializes in the development and manufacturing of complex aluminum castings for structural automotive applications. Its capabilities span the full engineering cycle, including R&D, die design, product design support, and process engineering, all performed in-house. The Shelbyville campus focuses on high-pressure die casting of aluminum alloys for safety-critical components.

Ryobi serves the global automotive industry, supplying major OEMs such as Honda and General Motors. In 2022, Honda recognized the company with its Excellence in Delivery and Quality award, and General Motors has named Ryobi a Supplier of the Year for five consecutive years.

Ryobi’s stated mission is to win the superior confidence of the die casting market through responsibility, quality communication, and customer service. Its corporate values—Communicate, Change, Can Do, Capable, Choose, Challenge, Committed, Contributions—underscore a culture of continuous improvement and partnership with both internal and external customers.

old_description: The company was founded in 1985 and our Quality Management System has been certified to both
about:
RDS Wire & Cable, Inc. was founded in 1985 in Gardena, California, where it continues to operate as a stocking distributor of electronic and electrical wire, cable, tubing, and sleeving.

The company maintains a broad inventory of UL AWM appliance wiring materials, MIL-spec military and aerospace wires (including MIL-C-27500, SAE AS22759, and MIL-W-16878 series), coaxial cables, heat-shrinkable tubing, braided sleeving, and fiberglass insulation. Value-added processing services include etching of fluoropolymer (Teflon) wire and tubing, hot marking of heat-shrink tubing, cutting, stripping, striping, tinning, high-speed twisting, and custom cable assembly per customer drawings.

Primary customers are military and aerospace contractors, as well as commercial equipment manufacturers requiring compliant wire and insulation solutions. The firm supplies products built to specifications such as MIL-C-17 coaxial cable, SAE AS23053 heat-shrink tubing, and UL styles 1007, 1015, 1571, and 1180.

RDS differentiates itself with low minimum-order quantities, fast order fulfillment, and an experienced sales staff supported by a quality management system certified to ISO 9001 and AS9100 since 2003. The company also offers RoHS, REACH, and conflict-minerals compliance documentation for regulated programs.

name: REM Electronics
old_description: REM specializes in sourcing and replacing obsolete or hard-to-find components, helping customers avoid costly downtime and keep production on track. With our expertise and commitment to continuity, REM is a trusted partner in maintaining efficient, uninterrupted operations.
about:
REM Electronics Supply Company, Inc. operates from Warren, Ohio, where it was founded in 1955 by Robert E. Miller. The business began as a sales and service operation focused on consumer-market TV antennas and hi-fi equipment before evolving into a broader electronics supplier.

Today the company provides full contract manufacturing, assembly, testing, and distribution from a combined office and warehouse footprint of 30,000 to 75,000 square feet. Its manufacturing services cover surface-mount and through-hole PCB assembly, cable and wire-harness assembly, 3D printing and prototyping, design assistance, component preparation and modification, X-ray inspection, and RFID integration.

REM serves U.S. government agencies involved in defense and national security, as well as manufacturers, assemblers, and repair teams across the electronics sector. The company emphasizes its ability to source or recreate obsolete and hard-to-find components to prevent production downtime.

The firm highlights its domestic production as a differentiator, stating that U.S.-based manufacturing ensures higher quality control, faster turnaround, and stronger supply-chain security for the defense customers it supports. Leadership frames the mission as honoring the founder’s legacy through competitive pricing and a commitment to customer service.

name: REV - Home Internet, TV, & Security
old_description: Since 1935, REV has been committed to not only being the best telecommunications provider but also to the growth and prosperity of South Louisiana. Through our involvement in and support of education, the arts, civic groups and non-profit organizations throughout South Louisiana, REV has always demonstrated its dedication to actively shaping and strengthening this special place we call home.
about:
REV, headquartered in Reserve, Louisiana, traces its roots to 1935 when it began as a local telephone provider. The company remains privately owned and operates as the largest private-owned telecommunications provider in Louisiana. In 2020, the business was reorganized under the REV brand, combining RTC, EATEL, EATEL Business, and Vision Communications into a single parent company.

REV delivers fiber-to-the-home internet, television, voice, and home security services across South Louisiana, backed by a network of more than 2,790 miles of fiber. The company also operates VENYU, a data center and cloud hosting division with facilities in Louisiana and nationwide. REV’s fiber network provides symmetrical upload and download speeds with no data caps, contracts, or installation fees, and includes managed WiFi using eero hardware.

The provider serves residential and business customers in the Baton Rouge, Bayou, River, and Capital regions, as well as the Shreveport/Bossier area. Its customer base exceeds 60,000 subscribers, ranging from households streaming video and gaming to enterprises requiring cloud hosting and data protection.

REV emphasizes its local commitment, reinvesting in the communities it serves through employee-directed philanthropic grants and partnerships with education, arts, and nonprofit organizations. The company says its differentiation lies in a locally staffed support model and a network built specifically for modern bandwidth demands.

name: REYcomp INC
old_description: We are your competent partner for electronic assemblies that range from surface mount (SMT) and through-hole (TH) as well as wire harnesses all the way to complete product box build services and panel assembly.
about:
REYcomp Inc. is an electronic contract manufacturer based in Grand Prairie, Texas, founded in 2001. The company is led by CEO Georg Rey and specializes in the miniaturization of printed circuit board assemblies.

The shop provides surface-mount (SMT) and through-hole (TH) assembly, wire-harness fabrication, full box-build and panel assembly, plus a repair service that covers even third-party products. Production runs on Siemens placement equipment capable of handling QFB, BGA, µBGA, CBDA, CSP and flip-chip packages. REYcomp employs cellular manufacturing, single-piece flow, standardized work and pull systems to compress lead times and eliminate excess inventory.

The company serves original equipment manufacturers across the electronics sector, supporting projects from prototype through volume production. Its repair and after-sales program extends the life cycle of deployed assemblies.

REYcomp emphasizes quick-turn responsiveness and a cost-performance ratio driven by direct engineer-to-engineer communication. As CEO Georg Rey puts it, the team avoids bureaucratic delays to move assemblies into production rapidly.

The company also supplies bank fixtures and cabinetry, nurses stations, and custom trade-show exhibits with crating.

RJ Wood stresses that its people and partnership approach set it apart, citing strategic customer relationships and project management as core differentiators.
